result.title: Knowledge Transfer for Conditional Flow Matching: Frozen Estimation and Adaptation
result.summary: Conditional generative modeling with limited target data can benefit from representations learned in a related source population. We develop a transfer learning framework for conditional flow matching that accommodates distinct source and target response distributions and dimensions. Two procedures exploit a representation learned from source data: TFM-Freeze estimates a target velocity head with the representation fixed, whereas TFM-Adapt jointly learns the head and a representation adaptation under a functional anchoring penalty. For explicit neural network classes, we establish bounds on conditional squared Wasserstein risk that account for source estimation, target fitting, representation mismatch, and numerical integration. When the source representation admits a smooth correction, adaptation replaces the frozen mismatch contribution by the cost of learning the correction and a controllable regularization bias. An information lower bound identifies regimes in which adaptation attains a strictly faster conditional squared Wasserstein risk rate than any generator restricted to the frozen context information. We also develop independent validation procedure for selecting among fitted conditional generators. We show that the selection procedure satisfies an oracle inequality, and the switching rule guarantees, with high probability, no increase in conditional energy risk relative to a target-only generator. Simulations and real data applications illustrate the gains from our proposed methods and the effectiveness of target validation in guarding against negative transfer.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为条件 flow matching 建立迁移学习框架，比较固定源表示的 TFM-Freeze 与带函数锚定惩罚联合适配的 TFM-Adapt，并给出条件平方 Wasserstein 风险界、信息下界以及用于选择生成器的目标域验证流程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结表示 vs 适配表示」的风险分解（源估计、目标拟合、表示错配）与用验证防负迁移的思路，可能为 LVR 中是否适配视觉表示、latent 证据是否真带来增益提供可核查的分析视角，但与多模态推理无直接联系。
